Keep one path and the shared checks. See the
[contributor lifecycle](https://github.com/Guust-Franssens/tableau-to-powerbi-migration/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#issue-to-pr-lifecycle).

## Operator/customer impact

- Why it matters: <!-- Concrete failure, confusion, risk, or wasted effort removed. Mechanical exception: repository-maintenance value only. -->
- Journey change: <!-- Observable before -> after. Mechanical exception: write "No direct operator/customer journey change - byte-local only." -->

## Behavioral change

- Issue: <!-- Fixes #N for a complete fix; Refs #N for partial work. -->
- Independent plan review: <!-- Link, verdict, and approved revision. -->
- Approved base SHA:
- Plan delta: <!-- None, or changed scope/shared files and renewed plan-review link. -->
- Acceptance results: <!-- Outcome, production-path reachability, whole claimed surface and controls: evidence -> verdict; disclose limits. -->

## Mechanical exception

Only byte-local changes with no runtime, policy, authority, safety, privacy, fidelity, data-loss,
or customer-facing consequence qualify. A one-line behavioral change is not mechanical.

- Byte-local justification (one sentence):
- Issue / plan review: <!-- Link if applicable; otherwise N/A with a reason. -->

## Required for either path

- Validation: <!-- Each command and exit code; name any skipped checks and why. -->
- [ ] Diff, issue/PR text and attachments contain no secrets or customer data, including identifying screenshots or personal machine paths.
- Blind diff review: <!-- Reviewer, link and verdict; issue/requirement + diff only, without the author's rationale. -->
- Exact reviewed head SHA:

Mechanical issue/plan fields may be N/A with a reason; the shared checks are never waived.
Any later commit makes the review stale: obtain a fresh blind review and record its exact head SHA
before merge.
